Indianapolis is the capital and most populous city of Indiana.
Indianapolis is situated in the central till plain region along the west fork of the White River.
The official slogan for Indianapolis is "Crossroads of America."
At the 2020 census, Indianapolis had a population of 887,642.
Indianapolis is the 16th-most populous city in the U.S.
Indianapolis is the third-most populous city in the Midwest after Chicago and Columbus, Ohio.
Indianapolis is the fourth-most populous state capital in the nation after Phoenix, Austin, and Columbus.
The Indianapolis metropolitan area is the 34th-most populous metropolitan statistical area in the U.S., with a population of 2.1 million residents.
With a combined statistical area population of over 2.6 million, Indianapolis ranks 27th.
Indianapolis proper covers 368 square miles (950 km²).
The city's land area is 19th-most extensive in the country by size.
Indigenous peoples inhabited the area dating back to as early as 10,000 BC.
In 1818, the Lenape relinquished their tribal lands in central Indiana under the Treaty of St. Mary's.
In 1821, Indianapolis was established as a planned city for the new seat of Indiana's state government.
The city was platted by Alexander Ralston and Elias Pym Fordham on a 1-square-mile (2.6 km²) grid.
Completion of the National and Michigan roads solidified Indianapolis's position as a major manufacturing and commercial center.
Since the 1970s, local government administration operates under Unigov, known as the consolidation of city-county governments.
Indianapolis anchors the 29th largest metropolitan economy in the U.S., with a gross domestic product of $184.4 billion in 2022.
The city's major exports include pharmaceuticals, motor vehicle parts, medical equipment and supplies, engine and power equipment, and aircraft products and parts.
Three Fortune 500 companies are based in Indianapolis: Elevance Health, Eli Lilly, and Corteva.

Other notable companies based in the city include AES Indiana, Allison Transmission, Barnes & Thornburg, Calumet, Inc., CountryMark, Emmis Corporation, Finish Line, Herff Jones, Klipsch Audio Technologies, Lids, OneAmerica Financial, Republic Airways Holdings, Simon Property Group, Steak 'n Shake, Sun King Brewing, Wheaton World Wide Moving, and Zipp.
FedEx employs 7,000 workers across 35 facilities in Indianapolis.
The city's central location and extensive highway and rail infrastructure have positioned it as an important logistics center.
Indianapolis is home to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, a National Historic Landmark and the world's largest sports venue by capacity with 235,000 permanent seats.
Since 1911, the Indianapolis 500 has been held at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway on Memorial Day weekend.
The race is considered the world's largest single-day sporting event and part of the Triple Crown of Motorsport.
Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park hosts the NHRA U.S. Nationals each Labor Day weekend.
Indianapolis is home to the Indianapolis Colts, a National Football League team.
The Indiana Pacers are based in Indianapolis, playing in the National Basketball Association (NBA).
The Indiana Fever play in the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA).
The Indianapolis Indians are a minor league baseball team in the International League.
Indy Eleven and Indy Fuel are professional soccer and ice hockey teams, respectively.
Indianapolis is known as the "Amateur Sports Capital of the World."
The NCAA and the National Federation of State High School Associations are based in Indianapolis.
Butler University's Hinkle Fieldhouse was a hub for Hoosier Hysteria, a general excitement for basketball throughout Indiana.
Hinkle Fieldhouse opened in 1928 as the world's largest basketball arena with seating for 15,000.
The Indiana High School Athletic Association is based in Indianapolis.
Indianapolis has an emerging food scene and established eateries like Long's Bakery, Mug-n-Bun, Shapiro's, and St. Elmo Steak House.
The Indianapolis Star is the city's primary daily newspaper.
Indianapolis Monthly, Indianapolis Business Journal, and NUVO are additional publications serving the city.
Jane Pauley and David Letterman launched their broadcasting careers in local television with WISH-TV and WTHR, respectively.
Dozens of commercial AM and FM radio stations serve the Indianapolis area.
The Indianapolis Motor Speedway Radio Network is broadcast from WFNI (formerly WIBC).
Public transportation in Indianapolis includes a local public bus system operated by IndyGo.
Indianapolis International Airport serves as the city's primary airport with connections to about 50 nonstop domestic and international destinations.
Geist Reservoir provides part of the city's water supply.
AES Indiana supplies electricity to over 500,000 customers in Indianapolis.
Citizens Energy Group manages natural gas, water, and wastewater utilities.
The Perry K. Generating Station produces steam for heating and cooling downtown Indianapolis.
Indianapolis has a sister city relationship with several cities worldwide.
